subject: Post-demo: clarification on DPA roles, logging retention, and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up + DPA clarifications from today's call

Hi Hannah — thanks for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups from my security and procurement teams: 

1) Roles: we need explicit confirmation in the DPA whether Redwood will be acting purely as a processor for Acme Health data, and whether any parts of processing could be considered controller-led (e.g., model training/updates from customer telemetry). Please point to the clause in your DPA draft that maps controller vs processor responsibilities.

2) Subprocessors: we need a current list of subprocessors and whether any EU-located subprocessors will have access to raw PII. We also need an option to receive 30 days notice prior to adding new subprocessors (Acme security req).

3) Breach notice timing: our legal requests a maximum 48-hour window for initial notification for incidents involving exfiltration of PII; can Redwood commit to that or do you have standard language (we heard 72 hours in the call)?

4) Logging & retention: we need details on what logs you retain (access logs, API request/response logs, KV cache traces) and default retention periods; specifically whether request-level logs storing prompts/responses are retained by default and how long.

5) Data residency: we plan to keep EU-sourced user records in EU-only model endpoints. Can you confirm you support region-locking and provide evidence of data residency controls?

Can you send the DPA draft and any evidence artifacts (SOC2, subprocessor csv) and a short answer to the 48-hour question? Our target is to include Redwood in our vendor security review this week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Integrations, Acme Health
jordan.lee@acmehealth.com

P.S. attaching the procurement checklist we use (not attached here) — happy to map answers directly onto it.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + DPA clarifications from today's call

Hi Jordan — great to meet you and the team today. Appreciate the clear list; answers below and next steps at the bottom. Attaching: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf and current subprocessor_list_2026-12.csv. Also linking a short SOC 2 summary (we can provide the full report under NDA).

1) Roles: Redwood operates as a processor per our standard DPA; we do not train customer-provided models on customer data unless separately contracted. See section 2 ("Data Roles") in the attached DPA which maps obligations. If you want we can add a short table in the DPA explicitly listing controller (Acme Health) vs processor (Redwood) responsibilities — happy to include if that helps procurement.

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV lists subprocessors and location. No EU subprocessor has access to raw customer PII for the standard hosted product; EU residency endpoints keep customer data within region unless explicitly routed. We can provide an auditable list and notify you of additions; our standard notice period is 30 days but we can discuss contractually requiring notice for specific classes of subprocessors.

3) Breach notice timing: our security practice is to provide initial notification "as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours" for incidents involving personal data; that is what our DPA currently states. I understand Acme's preference for 48 hours — I will flag this to legal and see whether we can accept a 48-hour initial notification for confirmed exfiltration events. If we can't, we can offer a contractual SLA for expedited notification for high-severity incidents.

4) Logging & retention: default collection includes API access logs, token usage metrics, and diagnostic traces. By default, request/response logs that may contain PII are retained for 30 days in hosted plans; for Dedicated/Private deployments retention can be configured and set to 0 days. We can provide a log-retention matrix and examples of redaction/field-level masking.

5) Data residency: yes, region-locking is supported via our Private/Dedicated options and via routing policies for hosted accounts. Attached are the residency controls summary and a link to the region configuration doc (see Drive link).

Next steps (proposed):
- Marissa (legal) will propose any DPA redlines by Wed EOD PT (cc'd).
- I'll follow up on the 48-hour ask and confirm whether we can do that for confirmed PII exfiltration events.
- If Acme wants SOC2 full report, we can deliver under NDA (Marissa can coordinate).

I'll be available for a quick call if you want to walk through the DPA mapping.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_list_2026-12.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: proposed DPA redlines & evidence checklist for Acme (DEAL-4589)

Hannah / Aditya — following up with suggested redlines and a short evidence list so we can move quickly on Acme's procurement timeline. Summary: Acme is pushing on 48-hour initial notification and wants contractual notice for new subprocessors. They also asked for a clearer controller/processor mapping in the DPA.

Actionable redlines (high-level):
- Add a 1-paragraph controller "mapping table" in Section 2 to make responsibilities explicit.
- For breach notify: propose two-tier approach: 72 hours default + language allowing 48-hour initial notification for confirmed PII exfiltration if we agree to a severity classification process (to avoid false positives). This is a compromise we can offer to mid-market customers.
- Subprocessor notice: offer 30 days notice + ability for Acme to object; if they object to a subprocessor with no alternative we can agree to remediation or escrow clause.

Evidence checklist to send to Acme (we should attach or link each):
- SOC2 Type II summary + full report under NDA (we can provide)
- Current subprocessor CSV (attached)
- Residency controls summary doc (link)
- Log retention matrix (show hosted default 30d, config options for Dedicated/Private)

Questions for engineering/legal:
- Can we commit to an agreed severity triage timeline for confirming PII exfiltration (to support 48-hour notify)? If not, we should keep 72 hours + expedited notification SLA for confirmed events.

I'll draft the redlines and send a tracked-changes DPA by EOD today. Setting target to have an exec-signed DPA in 10 business days to keep the deal on track.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarification on DPA roles, logging retention, and subprocessor evidence

Thanks Hannah and Marissa — good summary and appreciate the proposed compromise on notification timing. A few quick items to keep our procurement calendar moving: 

- Please send the SOC2 report under NDA (we'll send the NDA this afternoon).
- The subprocessor CSV looks fine; can you confirm whether any subprocessor has the ability to see raw prompt/response pairs? If yes, call that out explicitly.
- We're OK with the "72 hours default + 48 hours for confirmed PII exfiltration with a triage process" approach — please include that language in the redline.
- For logging: confirm that hosted default retention is 30 days for request-level logs and that Dedicated can be configured to reduce to 0 days. We'll include that in our security questionnaire.

If you can get the tracked DPA redlines and SOC2 under NDA by EOD tomorrow, procurement can move to legal review on Friday. Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

Best,
Jordan

--
Jordan Lee
Head of Integrations, Acme Health
jordan.lee@acmehealth.com
